title: ArachStudio
summary: Live-edit your GitHub components directly in the browser
content: ArachStudio : Live-edit your GitHub components directly in the browser | Product Hunt Launching today ArachStudio Launching today Live-edit your GitHub components directly in the browser 95 followers Live-edit your GitHub components directly in the browser 95 followers Visit website Code editors • AI Code Editors Hi Product Hunt! 👋 ArachStudio helps designers & developers live-edit codebases & components online. How it works: Connect GitHub via access token. Scan & load your project path. Make real-time style edits in the visual preview (desktop/mobile). Export the final product! Help us decide: We are testing two different demo versions. Try both links and tell us which experience you prefer in the comments! Overview Reviews Alternatives Built with Team More Interactive Payment Required Launch tags: Design Tools • Developer Tools • GitHub 1 month free Launch Team / Built With Show more Show more Launching Today # 25 Day Rank Upvote • 103 points Follow ArachStudio Add to collection Share Analytics Company Info arachstudio01.vercel.app ArachStudio Info Launched in 2026 Forum p/arachstudio Similar Products vscode.dev Bringing VS Code to the browser 4.9 ( 32 reviews ) Code editors v0 by Vercel Full stack vibe coding platform. Created by Vercel. 4.9 ( 56 reviews ) Engineering & Development AI Coding Agents Codux Visual IDE for React 5.0 ( 1 review ) Code editors Relate Create the web together 4.0 ( 1 review ) Design & Creative Code editors Locofy.ai Build frontend 10x faster with design-to-code AI 4.9 ( 35 reviews ) Automation tools AI Coding Agents View more Subscribe Sign in What do you think? … Login to comment Khajieh Manpourian ArachStudio Maker 📌 Hi Product Hunt! 👋 I’m Khajieh Manbourian, and I'm incredibly excited to share ArachStudio with you today. The inspiration for this tool actually came out of my own personal frustration. Just as Linus Torvalds built Git because he needed a better way to build Linux, I built ArachStudio out of sheer necessity while working on my other product, ArachTech. The Problem: I desperately needed a way to ship faster, perform live edits seamlessly, and speed up deployments. The traditional cycle of coding, previewing, and pushing just felt too slow and disconnected for the speed I wanted to move at. The Solution: I built ArachStudio to bridge that gap. It allows you to connect your GitHub repo and visually live-edit your components right in the browser. I designed this specifically for: "Vibe coders" who want to build and iterate quickly by feel. New web designers looking for an easier bridge into code. Component editors who need a frictionless way to develop, tweak, push, and deploy. I need your help! To get this right, I’ve included two different demo links in the launch above. I want to know which workflow and experience feels better to you. Please take both demos for a spin, test out the live editing, and let me know in the comments: Which version do you prefer and what feature should I build next? Thank you

CartAI completes checkout on any live merchant surface with no merchant-side work, cooperating with bot detection instead of evading it. One developer-first API, four products: Catalog (search and live pricing across merchants), Checkouts (clear and track orders to confirmation), Payments (PCI off your stack via Visa and Mastercard agent rails), Monetization (commissions on every agent sale). content: Diffsmith: Comment on your AI agent's code & collaborate on changes | Product Hunt Launching today Diffsmith Launching today Comment on your AI agent's code & collaborate on changes 107 followers Comment on your AI agent's code & collaborate on changes 107 followers Visit website Code Review Tools Diffsmith is a code review studio for local git changes made by Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, or any other AI coding agent. Open a repo, read the uncommitted diff, and click any line to leave a comment anchored to that exact spot. Then hand your notes straight back to the agent. Supports MCP for viewing you're agent's replies to your comments directly at the line of code it relates to. Diffsmith is 100% offline and a one time purchase unlocks lifetime access. The mechanic I want to understand: when the agent answers a comment by rewriting the whole block, where does the anchor go, does the comment follow the moved logic or die with the old lines? That resolution step decides whether review rounds stay readable after round three. Upvote Report Share 19h ago Max Chuquimia Maker @vollos Great question! In that situation, comments can’t stay with the new lines so they get archived into a “Past” tab in the sidebar (you can click it there to see the original lines it was anchored too). Agents can add a comment to the newly changed code if they want to (and in my experience they often do because they understand that the original comment will be archived) Upvote (1) Report Share 18h ago Chalermpon Ananwattanakit @maxchuquimia Archiving beats the pretend option, a comment glued to lines it no longer describes is worse than one that admits it's history. Agents leaving a fresh comment on the new code because they know the old one gets archived surprised me, that's the loop closing itself. Thanks Max. content: tterm: A terminal, a real browser, and Claude Code under one roof | Product Hunt Launching today tterm Launching today A terminal, a real browser, and Claude Code under one roof 133 followers A terminal, a real browser, and Claude Code under one roof 133 followers Visit website Terminals • AI Code Editors tterm is a macOS cockpit for working with Claude Code. Every project is a row of explorer, Claude, and file viewer. Stack as many as you're juggling. A real Chromium browser lives inside, and there's no editor on purpose: you review diffs hunk by hunk and commit. It even rebuilds itself. Ask the Claude pane for a feature and the running app hot-reloads with it. No account, no telemetry. Free for hobbyists, on Apple silicon. I built tterm because I was living in three windows: a terminal running Claude Code, a browser to check what it built, and an editor I barely typed in anymore. tterm folds them into one. Every project is a row of explorer, Claude, and file viewer. A real Chromium browser lives inside, with your Chrome bookmarks and cookies along for the ride. There's no editor on purpose: you review diffs hunk by hunk and commit. The fun part is that tterm builds itself. Most features shipped by asking the Claude pane running inside tterm, and the app hot-reloads. Even the landing page is in on it: the ocean is the word OCEAN riding a live wave simulation, and it reacts when you scroll. Free, no account, no telemetry. I'd love feedback! Upvote Report Share 3d ago Valeria That breakdown is exactly what I wanted — copy-once into tterm's own profile with a Keychain consent prompt is the clean answer. The part I'd still gate is the agent driving authenticated sessions: treating page text as untrusted data protects the model's reasoning, but a prompt-injected page could still steer it to navigate and submit somewhere I'm already logged in. Even before a full origin allowlist, would a read-only mode on authenticated origins (view but not click/submit) be feasible as a stopgap? Ditto takes any website and gives you back a clean copy in Next.js or Vite. We extract actual components, sections, design tokens, and an editable content model. We even do our best to get hover states, focus states, dropdowns, accordions, declaritive motion, web fonts, SEO metadata, lottie animations, and responsive layout. Ditto is fully deterministic, so it is fast, cheap, and consistent. An AI-based approach can't deliver this. Why open source? We've been running a version of ditto inside ion.design since the start of the year and it's a bit too useful to keep to ourselves. ditto is an extremely valuable starting point for AI builders, because you can get a ready-to-go clone of a customer's website as soon as they sign up rather than a blank canvas. What you get: 🧩 Clean, componentized Next.js or Vite + TypeScript. Optional Tailwind styling. 🎯 Deterministic. no AI guesswork, byte-stable output. 🔌 Free hosted REST API + MCP server, or self-host for best speed. 🎨 Tokens, interactions, hover states, fonts, SEO preserved. 🪪 MIT licensed, fully open source. Try it: https://ditto.site Star us: https://github.com/ion-design/di... We're around all day! Give it a spin, tear it apart, tell us what you want, and use the hell out of it. We're all in this together, let's create user value. 💚 - The

summary: Your Mac tidies itself: screenshots, installers, Downloads
content: Tidy: Your Mac tidies itself: screenshots, installers, Downloads | Product Hunt Launching today Tidy Launching today Your Mac tidies itself: screenshots, installers, Downloads 116 followers Your Mac tidies itself: screenshots, installers, Downloads 116 followers Visit website Automation tools Tidy lives in your menu bar and handles three chores you keep doing by hand. It archives new Desktop screenshots, renaming them from their content with on-device OCR — "Screenshot 14.22.10.png" becomes "invoice-march.png". It ejects thedmg you mounted and trashes the installer. It sorts new Downloads by type, with rules you write in plain English. Apple Intelligence builds them on-device, so nothing leaves your Mac. Only touches new files. Never deletes. $9 once, no subscription. Overview Reviews Alternatives Built with Team More Payment Required Launch tags: Mac • Productivity • Artificial Intelligence Launch Team / Built With Show more Show more Launching Today # 17 Day Rank Upvote • 122 points Follow Tidy Add to collection Share Analytics Company Info tidymacapp.com Tidy Info Launched in 2026 Forum p/tidy-5 Similar Products Riffo Fast, custom batch AI renaming for various file formats. 5.0 ( 4 reviews ) Automation tools AI Infrastructure Tools NudgeFile Automatically organize, rename, and manage files with AI 5.0 ( 1 review ) Automation tools Files Magic AI AI Agent for mac Productivity Automation tools Keyboard Maestro The Premiere Mac Automation Software 5.0 ( 1 review ) Automation tools Hazel Your personal housekeeper Automation tools File storage and sharing apps View more Subscribe Sign in Social X What do you think? … Login to comment Sebastián Díaz Thomas Maker 📌 Hi Product Hunt 👋 I built Tidy because three things kept eating my Desktop: screenshots, .dmg installers, and a Downloads folder I'd given up on. Funny thing happened while testing the checkout. I bought my own app, downloaded the .dmg, dragged it to Applications, opened it — then went looking for the installer to clean up. It was already in the Trash. Tidy had ejected the disk and trashed its own installer. Nobody told it to. That's just what it does. Two rules I set for myself: · Only touches NEW files — never your backlog. · Never deletes. Archives or trashes, always reversible. The plain-English rules run on Apple Intelligence, on-device — nothing leaves your Mac. That's also why it's $9 once, not a subscription: my marginal cost per user is zero. Happy to answer anything. Upvote (1) Report Share 5d ago Yuki_Code1 Auto-organizing Downloads and screenshots is one of those "small thing, huge relief" features.
